title: The Leader You Were
author: Dr. Cindy Foster Chance
summary: Cindy Foster Chance asks whether the leader you are now is simply the leader you used to be, and argues that past success can blind us to the moment an approach stops working. Drawing on her own experience of leading with trust and candor in a context where trust was impossible, she says the lesson was to refine her values, not abandon them. She applies the pattern to founders who have outgrown the way they run their businesses, describing three types: the leader who touches everything, the one who keeps accommodating, and the one who relies on lessons learned. Her answer is that growth needs insight into context, range, and attunement, with attunement to oneself being the hardest. She closes with four questions for diagnosing what is core, what still serves, what must change, and what stands in the way.
points: Success makes it hard to notice that a once-reliable approach no longer fits the context, and working harder only deepens the rut.
Changing how you lead can preserve who you are: the values stay, while the way of expressing them adapts to the situation.
Three founder patterns (touching everything, accommodating everyone, trusting old lessons) each foreclose growth in a different way.
Fear of change often masquerades as protection when it is really attachment to identity.
Because the people around a leader are poorly placed to name the problem, an outside thinking partner can help surface it.
quotes: When something has worked for you up until now, it is confusing to recognize that it no longer does. There is a big lesson in that confusion. If you have been successful and now find yourself struggling, what got you here will not move you forward.
Here is the thing: more effort does not move you forward. Working harder keeps you stuck, precisely because it means doing more of what you already know how to do.
What we don’t like to consider is that a great deal about who we are can change without destroying who we are. And many things that now seem non-negotiable in your business could change.
Your friendliness and flexibility built your reputation. Now they are killing you.
You are afraid it will break everything you built. That fear feels like protection. Often it is identity.
Attunement includes attunement to yourself. What do you really need? When the work that used to give you energy is draining you, that is information.
But aligning with your values does not mean insisting on them no matter what the world teaches you. The work is to find the path that aligns more effortlessly.
We can’t easily see our own comfortable habits. That is human nature. They don’t feel like habits; they feel like who we are.
